Marta (Eng): Hey team — heads up I'm relocating to Toronto next month (work visa). Quick Qs about benefits: can I keep contributing to the US 401(k) while working from Canada? Also will I still be eligible for HSA contributions if I'm technically no longer a US resident for tax purposes?

Liam (People Ops): Congrats on the move! :tada: Short answer: usually no on ongoing 401(k) payroll contributions once you're moved and on Canadian payroll, and HSA eligibility often changes. But need to confirm with payroll + benefits vendor and tax. Can you share your expected move date?

Marta (Eng): Move date is 2026-04-15. We'll still have me on Redwood payroll until end of month, then I expect local Canadian payroll to start 2026-05-01. Also curious about rollover options if I stop contributions.

Ben (Benefits): Hi Marta — good questions. High-level: 1) If you're paid on a Canadian payroll (CRA taxed), US pre-tax 401(k) salary deferrals can't continue via Redwood payroll. 2) You can keep your balance in the 401(k) plan and later roll it to an IRA or another eligible plan. 3) Regarding HSA: contributions require US HDHP coverage and US tax status; moving abroad typically ends HSA eligibility.

Ben (Benefits): I'll check plan docs (Fidelity) for any passive contribution exceptions but we shouldn't assume contributions can continue while on foreign payroll. If you want, we can start a rollover packet + illustrate tax implications.

Marta (Eng): OK thanks. What's the process to stop contributions smoothly so there's no double-withholding during the payroll handoff?

Carlos (Payroll): @Marta (Eng) — timeline/steps: 1) Last US pay period that should have 401(k) deferrals is the pay dated 2026-04-30. 2) Submit deferral change to 0% effective 2026-04-30 in Workday before payroll cutoff. 3) Flag international assignment in Workday so we stop US tax withholding and export to global payroll. 4) For HSA, stop pre-tax HSA contribution elections same cutoff.

Carlos (Payroll): Example note to include in Workday: "Relocating to Canada — change 401(k) and HSA deferrals to 0% effective pay period ending 2026-04-30. Start Canadian payroll 2026-05-01." If you want I can walk through the Workday screens.

Marta (Eng): Perfect — I'll submit the changes this week. Regarding rollover: any reason to roll to a US IRA vs leaving in plan? Tax/regulatory tradeoffs?

Ben (Benefits): Pros/cons quick: leaving in Fidelity plan maintains continuity and often lower fees; rolling to a traditional IRA gives you control but may affect access to loans and different fee schedule. From benefits side we can leave it in-plan indefinitely (many expats do). For tax-specific advice (cross-border), we recommend consulting a cross-border tax advisor — we can share a vendor list if helpful.

Marta (Eng): Yes please share vendor list — also do we need a paper form or is Fidelity portal enough to request a distribution/rollover later?

Ben (Benefits): Fidelity portal supports rollovers/distributions; some transactions require signed forms for non-US addresses. I'll email the export checklist and link to the Fidelity rollover page.

Liam (People Ops): Action items: @Marta — submit Workday election changes before payroll cutoff; @Carlos — confirm we mark termination of US tax withholding and set up global payroll handoff; @Ben — send vendor list + Fidelity notes to Marta. I'll follow up once payroll confirms.

Marta (Eng): Thanks all! Appreciate the clear steps. :)

benefits-bot: NOTE: Per plan policy, non-US payroll assignments may affect eligibility and contribution options. See internal doc: https://intranet.redwood/bens/intl-relocation for details.
